newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK police deny knowledge of "IRA attack" report.
newsitem.headline: HK police deny knowledge of "IRA attack" report.

text.p: Hong Kong police denied knowledge of any Irish Republican Army (IRA) plan to target British dignitaries at the handover-to-China ceremony later on Monday to target. The Hong Kong Standard said on Monday police had carried out an overnight search of the Convention and Exhibition Centre venue after reports the IRA planned to attack British VIPs, but it gave no further details.
"We haven't heard about that," said duty officer Raymond Siu, Hong Kong police information officer, adding that the police did not comment on "newspaper speculation".
Security will be intense when British royal heir Prince Charles formally hands Hong Kong to Chinese President Jiang Zemin at midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday.
The handover will also be attended by Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen, British Prime Minister Tony Blair, and U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.
More than 4,000 VIPs are due to crowd into the Convention Centre's Grand Hall. Police sealed a security zone around the handover venue late on Sunday.

Security is also tight around the hotel where the Chinese leaders are expected to stay, with more than 24 officers guarding the hotel at the waterfront, and marine police in combat fatigues guarding a nearby pier.
Police earlier dealt with an alert when smoke billowed out of five of seven canisters they found late on Sunday next to a flower bed near the Convention Centre.
The contents were identified as hydrochloric acid used for cleaning, which police said was left behind by workers who constructed the centre.
